messages:
oncall-bot: PAGE: KV cache fragmentation spike detected on prod-us-west-2 (kv-pool-7). Severity: P1. Symptoms: high eviction rate, continuous-batching backlog, elevated malloc retry errors. Alert → https://incidents.redwood/INC-2028-kv-frag
sofia: ack, grabbing it. I'll triage root vs allocator. tagging @raj for allocator/PyTorch tuning ideas.
raj: looking — initial guess: CUDA/pyTorch allocator churn + large variable-length sequences causing slab fragmentation. will pull pmap logs.
sofia: quick customer impact — @mike-cs?
mike-cs: seeing 3 paying customers with increased 5xx and slower token p50 -> 210ms -> 520ms on their dedicated pools. CS escalations opened for two customers. Not yet billing impact but sessions are timing out.
sofia: ok ty. first steps: reduce continuous batching to stop batch growth, and roll a small config to force earlier KV compaction. doing a canary to 3 pods.
infra-ci: scheduling canary patch on kv-runtime-prod (namespace: prod) -> command: \n```\nkubectl -n prod set env deploy/kv-runtime CONT_BATCH_ENABLED=false KV_CACHE_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD=0.25\nkubectl rollout restart deploy/kv-runtime --selector=role=kv-canary\n```\nCanary started on 3/20 nodes.
kevin: non-blocking question — do we have a quick metric to watch to confirm reduced fragmentation? eviction rate + per-gpu free-memory-variance. Also watch p50 tokens and stream backpressure.
sofia: watching metrics: pre-change eviction rate avg 68% across pool. memory variance 0.72. errors: repeated cudaMalloc retries in logs.
sofia: applying canary now.
(oncall-bot automated): change deployed to canary nodes 3/20 at 2087654355 by infra-ci. Runbook: if eviction_rate drops < 30% within 5m mark as mitigated.
raj: also pushing a hotfix suggestion — set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 on runtime process to reduce large-slab splitting. Suggest setting MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 for jemalloc to reduce per-thread arenas. Example envs: \n```\nPYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64\nMALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2\n```\nThis should reduce fragmentation but may increase contention; prefer after immediate stabilization.
sofia: canary metrics coming in: eviction rate on canaries fell 68% -> 19% within 4m. p50 for canary pods improved ~180ms -> 210ms (slightly higher lat but stable), errors down. Good sign.
mike-cs: customers on canary nodes reporting reduced 5xx. one still seeing slow tail.
sofia: rolling patch to remaining nodes (gradual 5-node slices) — will also add the PYTORCH var as a staged change after rollout.
infra-ci: rolling out to remaining nodes in groups of 5, 40s between groups. Command logged at 2087654390.
sofia: putting a temporary rule to throttle continuous-batching window to 50ms globally to reduce join latency for KV writes: set REDWOOD_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=50 on runtime.
kevin: FYI, turning off continuous batching increases per-request latency but reduces memory blowups. acceptable trade for now.
raj: after full rollout, we should run arena compaction job and then run a targeted canary that sets MALLOC_ARENA_MAX and PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF — plan below.\n```\n# plan: post-stabilize (no elevated evictions for 10m)\n1) run per-node jemalloc purge/compaction via admin endpoint (kv-admin/compact)\n2) deploy PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF + MALLOC_ARENA_MAX to 30% nodes, monitor fragmentation\n3) if stable -> promote cluster-wide\n```\nsofia: rollout completed at 2087654455. cluster-level eviction rate dropped from 68% -> 22% in 10m. error rate normalized to baseline for most customers.
mike-cs: two customers still on dedicated reserved capacity clusters saw intermittent spikes; CS is following up but no new escalations.
raj: starting compaction job now (kv-admin/compact) on nodes in waves to avoid CPU spikes.
infra-ci: compaction job executed 2087654498 on 5 nodes. Logs show freed pages and reduced fragmentation score metric.
sofia: observed fragmentation metric drop (per-node fragmentation score) median 0.42 -> 0.18 after compaction + env changes. Good.
kevin: ops note — opened a ticket to instrument continuous-batching queue lengths per-tenant to avoid one noisy tenant causing cluster-wide growth. (#OPS-1429)
sofia: handoff to @kevin for overnight. Summary: cause = allocator + continuous-batching interaction producing KV cache blowups and slab fragmentation; immediate mitigation = disable cont-batching + KV compaction threshold, roll PYTORCH alloc conf and jemalloc arena change; customer impact mitigated but monitoring. Outstanding: monitor compaction stability, instrument per-tenant queueing, postmortem.
kevin: ack taking over. I'll keep watch for the next 6h and run the staged jemalloc rollout if stable for 30m. Escalate if eviction_rate > 40% or errors spike.
sofia: thanks — linking incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2028-kv-frag (creating postmortem). tagging #postmortems. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2028 created at 2087654322, P1 -> assigned to oncall.
kevin: quick note for handoff log: outstanding action items: (1) monitor eviction_rate and per-gpu free memory variance (2) schedule jemalloc/PyTorch env rollout (3) follow up with CS on two affected customers. I'll update after 30m.
sofia: leaving channel, ping me if it regresses.
kevin: will do, thanks!
